fact: The Ministry of Digital Transition's national data governance strategy SNGD 2030 sets as a principle that all data classified as critical information infrastructure must be processed and stored inside Côte d'Ivoire, by staff at least 20% Ivorian, with a copy kept in the country for law enforcement; the document gives no date of its own, so its published date of 2024-01-01 is used.

The national data governance strategy and AI strategy, handed to the Prime Minister on 13 March 2025 and awaiting government adoption, call for data centres and sovereign clouds to host and secure the country's data locally.

fact: Minister Ibrahim Kalil Konate, visiting the national data centre at VITIB Grand-Bassam (CFA 42.361 billion, over 20% built), said it will securely host the State's strategic data as part of the country's digital sovereignty strategy.

Minister Ibrahim Kalil Konaté said at the 14 December 2023 first-stone ceremony that the national data centre, to host the data of national administrative bodies, symbolises the quest for digital sovereignty; Digital Mag says it has since stalled past its December 2024 delivery date.
The minister announced on 20 May 2025 the coming launch of a first national sovereign data centre to host the state's critical platforms and e-government services.
